nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: List Major Nutrients
nodes.outcome: List carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, and minerals as the major nutrients in food

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Test for Starch
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate the presence of starch in a food item by observing a blue-black colour change with dilute iodine solution

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Test for Protein
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate the presence of protein in a food sample using copper sulphate solution and caustic soda to produce a violet colour

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Test for Fats
nodes.outcome: Identify the presence of fat in a food item by detecting a translucent oily patch on paper

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Energy Giving Nutrients
nodes.outcome: Compare carbohydrates and fats as energy providers, identifying fats as providing more energy per unit amount

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Carbohydrate Sources
nodes.outcome: Identify common food sources rich in carbohydrates such as rice, wheat, potatoes, and maize

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Fat Sources
nodes.outcome: Classify sources of fats into plant sources like nuts and oils, and animal sources like butter and ghee

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Role of Proteins
nodes.outcome: Explain the role of proteins as body-building foods needed for growth and tissue repair

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Protein Sources
nodes.outcome: List plant sources such as pulses and beans, and animal sources such as milk, eggs, and fish, as rich in proteins

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Role of Vitamins
nodes.outcome: State the role of vitamins in protecting the body against diseases and keeping eyes, bones, teeth, and gums healthy

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Roles of Specific Vitamins
nodes.outcome: Describe specific roles of Vitamin A for skin and eye health, Vitamin C for fighting infections, and Vitamin D for calcium usage

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Role of Minerals
nodes.outcome: Identify essential minerals including calcium, phosphorus, iron, and iodine and their role in overall growth and maintenance

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Function of Dietary Fibre
nodes.outcome: Explain the importance of dietary fibres (roughage) in adding bulk to food and helping the body get rid of undigested food

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Sources of Dietary Fibre
nodes.outcome: Identify whole grains, pulses, fresh fruits, and vegetables as the main sources of dietary fibre

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Functions of Water in Body
nodes.outcome: State the functions of water in absorbing nutrients from food and throwing out wastes as urine and sweat

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Balanced Diet
nodes.outcome: Define a balanced diet as a diet providing all essential nutrients, roughage, and water in the right quantities

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Plan Cost-Effective Balanced Meal
nodes.outcome: Design a balanced meal plan using inexpensive local ingredients like pulses, fermented food, sprouted seeds, and seasonal vegetables

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Cause of Obesity
nodes.outcome: Explain how consuming an excess of fat-rich foods leads to obesity

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Nutrient Loss from Cooking and Washing
nodes.outcome: Identify that repeated washing of rice/pulses and excessive heat during cooking lead to loss of vitamins and minerals

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Concept of Deficiency Diseases
nodes.outcome: Define deficiency diseases as disorders caused by a prolonged lack of one or more nutrients in the diet

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Vitamin A Deficiency Symptoms
nodes.outcome: Match Vitamin A deficiency with night blindness and symptoms such as poor vision in darkness

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Vitamin B1 Deficiency and Beriberi
nodes.outcome: Identify beriberi as the deficiency disease of Vitamin B1 and name its symptoms of weak muscles and low energy

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Vitamin C Deficiency and Scurvy
nodes.outcome: Identify scurvy as the deficiency disease of Vitamin C and recognize symptoms like bleeding gums and delayed wound healing

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Deficiencies of Vitamin D and Calcium
nodes.outcome: Correlate Vitamin D deficiency with rickets (bent, soft bones) and calcium deficiency with weak bones and tooth decay

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Deficiencies of Iodine and Iron
nodes.outcome: Match iodine deficiency with goitre (swollen neck gland) and iron deficiency with anaemia (general body weakness)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Distinguish Objects from Materials
nodes.outcome: Distinguish between an object and the material it is made of using everyday examples

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Single Object Made of Multiple Materials
nodes.outcome: Identify different materials that combine to make a single object, such as a pencil made of wood, graphite, and rubber

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Multiple Objects from One Material
nodes.outcome: List several different objects that can be manufactured from a single material like wood, plastic, or iron

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Same Object Made from Different Materials
nodes.outcome: Give examples of a single kind of object that can be made from different materials, such as a tumbler made of glass, plastic, or metal

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Classify Objects by Material
nodes.outcome: Group a given set of household objects based on the primary material they are made of

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Purpose of Grouping Materials
nodes.outcome: State the advantages of grouping materials and objects based on convenience and studying their properties

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Lustre
nodes.outcome: Define lustre as the natural shine or gloss present on the freshly cut surface of certain materials

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Classify by Lustre
nodes.outcome: Classify given materials into lustrous (such as metals) and non-lustrous (such as wood or cardboard)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Loss of Lustre in Metals
nodes.outcome: Explain why metals often lose their shine and appear dull when exposed to air and moisture over time

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Hardness by Scratching and Compressing
nodes.outcome: Distinguish between hard and soft materials based on whether they can be easily compressed or scratched

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Classify Materials as Hard or Soft
nodes.outcome: Classify everyday substances into hard (like iron and stone) and soft (like cotton and sponge)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Soluble and Insoluble Substances
nodes.outcome: Define soluble substances as those that completely dissolve in water, and insoluble substances as those that do not

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Test Solubility of Solid Substances
nodes.outcome: Identify whether common solid substances like salt, sugar, sand, chalk powder, and sawdust are soluble or insoluble in water

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Test Miscibility of Liquids in Water
nodes.outcome: Classify liquids such as vinegar, lemon juice, mustard oil, and kerosene based on whether they mix completely with water or form a separate layer

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Solubility of Gases in Water
nodes.outcome: Identify that some gases like oxygen dissolve in water to support aquatic life, whereas other gases do not

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Observe Floating and Sinking in Water
nodes.outcome: Identify whether an insoluble material floats on the surface of water or sinks to the bottom

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Classify Objects by Floating and Sinking
nodes.outcome: Classify given objects like dry leaves, wood, stones, iron nails, and plastic balls into those that float and those that sink in water

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Transparent Materials
nodes.outcome: Define transparent materials as substances through which things can be seen clearly because light passes through them

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Opaque Materials
nodes.outcome: Define opaque materials as substances through which you cannot see anything because light cannot pass through them

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Translucent Materials
nodes.outcome: Define translucent materials as substances through which objects can be seen, but not clearly

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Classify Objects by Transparency
nodes.outcome: Classify items such as clear glass, butter paper, cardboard, clear water, and a wooden board as transparent, translucent, or opaque

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Demonstrate Translucency via Oil Patch
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate that an oily patch on paper makes the paper translucent by observing a light source through it

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Match Material Properties to Function
nodes.outcome: Explain why a specific material is chosen for an object based on its properties, such as why cooking pots are made of metal rather than paper

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Sort Materials by Multiple Properties
nodes.outcome: Categorize an unknown material using a combination of properties including lustre, hardness, solubility, flotation, and transparency

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Need for Separation
nodes.outcome: State reasons for separating components of a mixture, including removing harmful substances and obtaining useful components

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Principle of Handpicking
nodes.outcome: Identify handpicking as a separation method suitable when impurities differ in size, shape, or colour and are present in small quantities

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Application of Handpicking
nodes.outcome: Apply handpicking to separate visible stone pieces and husk from grain samples like rice or pulses

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Principle of Threshing
nodes.outcome: Describe threshing as the process of beating dry stalks to free the attached grains

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Methods of Threshing
nodes.outcome: Compare manual beating, using bullocks, and using motorized threshers for threshing large quantities of harvest

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Principle of Winnowing
nodes.outcome: Explain how winnowing separates heavier and lighter components of a dry mixture using wind or blowing air

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Application of Winnowing
nodes.outcome: Predict the separation pattern of husk particles from grain seeds during winnowing in the presence of wind

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Principle of Sieving
nodes.outcome: Explain how a sieve allows particles smaller than the mesh pore size to pass while retaining larger particles

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Applications of Sieving
nodes.outcome: Identify everyday applications of sieving, such as separating bran from flour and pebbles from sand at construction sites

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Selecting Dry Separation Methods
nodes.outcome: Select the most appropriate dry separation technique (handpicking, threshing, winnowing, or sieving) based on differences in size and weight of particles

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Sedimentation Process
nodes.outcome: Define sedimentation as the settling down of heavier, insoluble solid particles at the bottom of a liquid mixture

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Decantation Process
nodes.outcome: Describe decantation as the careful pouring out of the upper clear liquid layer without disturbing the settled sediment

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Decantation of Immiscible Liquids
nodes.outcome: Apply decantation to separate a mixture of two immiscible liquids that form distinct layers, such as oil and water

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Principle of Filtration
nodes.outcome: Explain how filtration uses a porous medium to separate fine insoluble solid particles from a liquid

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Assembling a Filter Paper Cone
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate the folding of a circular filter paper into a cone and fitting it inside a funnel for filtration

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Filtrate and Residue
nodes.outcome: Identify the substance retained on the filter as residue and the liquid that passes through as filtrate

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Evaporation for Separation
nodes.outcome: Define evaporation as the process of converting a liquid into its vapour to recover dissolved solid solutes

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Salt Harvesting by Evaporation
nodes.outcome: Explain how common salt is harvested by trapping seawater in shallow pits (lagoons) and allowing sunlight to evaporate the water

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Condensation Process
nodes.outcome: Define condensation as the process of converting water vapour into its liquid form upon cooling

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Combined Evaporation and Condensation
nodes.outcome: Trace the path of water vaporising and condensing on a cold metal plate to recover pure water from a salt-water solution

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Multi-step Separation Sequence
nodes.outcome: Order sequential separation steps (dissolution, decantation/filtration, and evaporation) to separate a complex mixture like sand and salt

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Definition of Saturated Solution
nodes.outcome: Define a saturated solution as one in which no more solute can dissolve at a given fixed temperature

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Effect of Temperature on Solubility
nodes.outcome: Explain how heating allows more solute to dissolve in a saturated solution, and cooling causes excess dissolved solute to separate out

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Comparing Solute Capacities
nodes.outcome: Compare the different maximum amounts of distinct solutes (e.g., salt vs sugar) that dissolve in an equal volume of water

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Characteristics of Herbs
nodes.outcome: Identify herbs by their short height, green stems, and tender branches

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Characteristics of Shrubs
nodes.outcome: Identify shrubs by their medium height, hard but not very thick stems branching near the base

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Characteristics of Trees
nodes.outcome: Identify trees by their tall height, thick, brown, woody stems with branches high above the ground

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Classify Herbs, Shrubs, and Trees
nodes.outcome: Classify given plant examples into herbs, shrubs, or trees based on physical features

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Differentiate Creepers and Climbers
nodes.outcome: Distinguish between creepers that spread on the ground and climbers that take support to climb up

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Stem Water Conduction Experiment
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate that stems conduct water using a stem placed in coloured water

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Trace Water Path Through Stem
nodes.outcome: Trace the upward movement of water and dissolved minerals through narrow tubes inside the stem to leaves

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Parts of a Leaf
nodes.outcome: Identify and label the petiole, lamina, veins, and midrib of a leaf

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Compare Leaf Venation Types
nodes.outcome: Distinguish between reticulate venation (net-like) and parallel venation in leaves

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Transpiration
nodes.outcome: State that transpiration is the release of water vapour by leaves into the air

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Demonstrate Transpiration Experimentally
nodes.outcome: Explain the appearance of water droplets inside an enclosed polythene bag tied around a leafy branch

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Inputs and Outputs of Photosynthesis
nodes.outcome: List sunlight, chlorophyll, water, and carbon dioxide as requirements, and oxygen and food (starch) as products of photosynthesis

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Test Starch in Green Leaves
nodes.outcome: Apply iodine solution to a decolourized leaf to verify the synthesis of starch by photosynthesis

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Functions of Roots
nodes.outcome: State the primary functions of roots as anchoring the plant firmly in soil and absorbing water and minerals

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Compare Taproot and Fibrous Roots
nodes.outcome: Compare taproots (having a main taproot and lateral roots) with fibrous roots (a cluster of similar-sized roots)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Correlate Venation with Root Type
nodes.outcome: Predict the root type of an intact plant from its leaf venation (reticulate with taproot, parallel with fibrous root)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Sepals and Petals
nodes.outcome: Identify sepals (outer green leaf-like parts) and petals (prominent coloured parts) in a flower

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Parts of a Stamen
nodes.outcome: Identify the two parts of a stamen: anther and filament

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Parts of a Pistil
nodes.outcome: Identify the three main parts of the pistil: stigma, style, and ovary

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Structure of Ovary and Ovules
nodes.outcome: Identify small bead-like structures called ovules inside a longitudinal or transverse section of an ovary

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Dissect and Label Flower Whorls
nodes.outcome: Separate and label all four main whorls (sepals, petals, stamens, and pistil) in a dissected flower

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Trace Water Path Through Whole Plant
nodes.outcome: Trace the continuous path of water from soil absorption by roots, upward conduction through stem, to transpiration and photosynthesis in leaves

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Definition of Joint
nodes.outcome: Define a joint as a place where two or more bones meet in the human body

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Ball and Socket Joint
nodes.outcome: Identify shoulder and hip joints as ball and socket joints that allow movement in all directions

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Pivotal Joint Structure and Movement
nodes.outcome: Describe the pivotal joint between the neck and head that allows forward-backward bending and left-right turning

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Hinge Joint Structure and Movement
nodes.outcome: Identify elbow and knee joints as hinge joints that allow back-and-forth movement in one plane only

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Fixed Joints in Skull
nodes.outcome: Identify fixed joints in the cranium/upper jaw where bones cannot move relative to one another

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Compare Joint Ranges of Motion
nodes.outcome: Compare the range of motion among ball-and-socket, pivotal, hinge, and fixed joints

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Functions of Human Skeleton
nodes.outcome: State the main functions of the human skeleton: framework shape, organ protection, and movement support

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Rib Cage Structure and Function
nodes.outcome: Describe the cone-shaped rib cage formed by 12 pairs of ribs joined to the chest bone and backbone protecting the heart and lungs

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Backbone Structure and Function
nodes.outcome: Explain how the backbone consists of 33 small vertebrae allowing flexibility and protecting the spinal cord

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Shoulder and Pelvic Bones
nodes.outcome: Identify shoulder bones and pelvic bones and state their role in enclosing and supporting lower body organs

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Cartilage Properties and Locations
nodes.outcome: Locate cartilage in the ear pinna, nose tip, and joint surfaces, noting it is softer and more flexible than bone

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Muscle Contraction and Relaxation
nodes.outcome: Describe how a muscle becomes shorter, thicker, and harder during contraction, pulling on a bone

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Antagonistic Muscle Pairs Action
nodes.outcome: Explain how a pair of antagonistic muscles (like biceps and triceps) work together by alternate contraction and relaxation to move a bone

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Earthworm Body Structure
nodes.outcome: Identify that an earthworm has no bones and consists of rings joined end to end with tiny bristles (setae)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Earthworm Locomotion Mechanism
nodes.outcome: Explain the wave-like contraction and expansion of circular and longitudinal muscles coupled with bristle anchoring that drives earthworm locomotion

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Snail Shell and Muscular Foot Structure
nodes.outcome: Identify the snail's outer shell as a non-bony exoskeleton and describe the thick muscular foot emerging from it

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Snail Locomotion via Muscular Foot
nodes.outcome: Describe how a snail moves by producing wavy muscular contractions and a slimy mucus trail along its muscular foot

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Cockroach Exoskeleton and Appendages
nodes.outcome: Identify the hard outer exoskeleton, three pairs of legs, and two pairs of wings attached to the breast of a cockroach

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Cockroach Walking and Flying Mechanics
nodes.outcome: Explain how distinct breast muscles coordinated with legs and wings enable a cockroach to walk, climb, and fly

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Skeletal Adaptations of Birds
nodes.outcome: List skeletal adaptations of birds for flight, including hollow lightweight bones and forelimbs modified into wings

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Flight Muscles and Breastbone in Birds
nodes.outcome: Explain how modified breastbones hold powerful flight muscles used to flap wings up and down during bird flight

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Streamlined Body Shape of Fish
nodes.outcome: Define a streamlined shape (tapering at both head and tail) and explain how it minimizes water resistance during swimming

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Fish Swimming Mechanics via Fins and Body Curves
nodes.outcome: Describe how alternating side-to-side body curves combined with caudal and paired fin movements propel and balance a fish in water

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Snake Locomotion via Lateral Loops
nodes.outcome: Explain how a long backbone and interconnected thin muscles curve a snake's body into multiple lateral loops that press against the ground to push it forward

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Habitat
nodes.outcome: Define a habitat as the physical surroundings or environment where an organism naturally lives and survives.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Biotic and Abiotic Components
nodes.outcome: Classify elements of an ecosystem into biotic components (living organisms) and abiotic components (non-living physical factors like rocks, soil, air, water, and sunlight).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Adaptation
nodes.outcome: Define adaptation as the presence of specific features or habits that enable an organism to naturally live in its habitat over thousands of years.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Adaptation vs Acclimatisation
nodes.outcome: Distinguish between adaptation (long-term evolutionary changes over generations) and acclimatisation (short-term physiological adjustments by an individual organism to overcome changes in surroundings).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Camel Adaptations in Deserts
nodes.outcome: List the structural adaptations of camels for desert survival, including long legs, concentrated urine, dry dung, lack of sweat, and fat storage in humps.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Desert Small Animal Adaptations
nodes.outcome: Explain how small desert animals such as rats and snakes stay cool during the day by staying in deep burrows and coming out only at night.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Cactus Structural Adaptations
nodes.outcome: Describe the structural adaptations of desert plants like cacti, including leaves modified into spines to reduce transpiration, photosynthetic stems covered with a thick waxy layer, and deep roots.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Mountain Tree Adaptations
nodes.outcome: Identify how cone-shaped branching and needle-like leaves help mountain trees shed rainwater and snow easily.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Mountain Animals Cold Adaptations
nodes.outcome: Explain how thick skin, dense fur, or layers of wool protect mountain animals like snow leopards, yaks, and mountain goats from extreme cold.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Mountain Goat Hoof Adaptation
nodes.outcome: Explain the role of strong hooves in mountain goats for running up rocky, steep slopes.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Grassland Predator Adaptations in Lions
nodes.outcome: Describe the adaptations of predators like lions in grasslands, including light brown camouflage color, eyes in front of the head for depth perception, and sharp retractable claws.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Grassland Prey Adaptations in Deer
nodes.outcome: Describe the adaptations of prey like deer in grasslands, including strong teeth for chewing hard plant stems, long ears for hearing predators, eyes on the sides of the head to look in all directions, and fast running speed.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Fish Adaptations for Water
nodes.outcome: List the key adaptations of fish for aquatic survival: streamlined body shape, slippery scales, fins and flat tails for balance and direction, and gills to extract dissolved oxygen from water.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Squid and Octopus Adaptations
nodes.outcome: Explain how squids and octopuses adapt to sea life by staying deep near the seabed, making their bodies streamlined when moving, and using gills to breathe dissolved oxygen.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Dolphin and Whale Respiration
nodes.outcome: Explain how whales and dolphins breathe atmospheric air through blowholes or nostrils located on the upper parts of their heads without using gills.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Floating Aquatic Plant Adaptations
nodes.outcome: Describe the adaptations of floating aquatic plants, such as highly reduced roots primarily for anchorage, hollow light stems, and broad leaves covered with a waxy coating.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Submerged Aquatic Plant Adaptations
nodes.outcome: Describe the adaptations of completely submerged aquatic plants, including narrow ribbon-like leaves and highly divided leaf structures that bend easily without breaking in flowing water.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Frog Adaptations for Land and Water
nodes.outcome: Identify the adaptations of frogs that allow them to live both in water and on land, including strong back legs for leaping and webbed feet for swimming.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Nutrition and Growth in Living Organisms
nodes.outcome: Explain how the requirements for food/nutrition and irreversible growth from young stages to adult stages characterize all living organisms.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Respiration in Living Organisms
nodes.outcome: Explain respiration as the process by which living organisms take in oxygen to release energy from food, producing carbon dioxide as a byproduct.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Stimulus and Response in Organisms
nodes.outcome: Define stimuli and provide examples of responses to stimuli in both animals (flinching from sharp objects) and plants (Mimosa leaves folding upon touch, flowers opening at sunrise).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Excretion in Plants and Animals
nodes.outcome: Define excretion as the process of getting rid of toxic wastes produced by life processes, and compare how animals eliminate wastes with plant mechanisms like storing secretions or shedding leaves.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Reproduction in Living Organisms
nodes.outcome: Compare reproduction methods across organisms, distinguishing between animals that lay eggs versus give birth to young, and plants that reproduce through seeds versus vegetative parts like tubers and cuttings.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Movement in Plants vs Animals
nodes.outcome: Compare locomotion from place to place in animals with internal transport and directional growth movements towards light or water in anchored plants.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Early Modes of Transport
nodes.outcome: Identify walking, animal-drawn carts, and simple hollowed-log boats as ancient modes of transport

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Impact of Wheel Invention
nodes.outcome: Explain how the invention of the wheel transformed transport efficiency and vehicle design

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Steam Engine Transport Revolution
nodes.outcome: Describe the transition from animal-driven vehicles to steam-powered railways and ships

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Chronological Sequence of Transport
nodes.outcome: Order modes of transportation chronologically from animal carts to steam engines, automobiles, aircraft, and high-speed electric trains

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Concept of Measurement
nodes.outcome: Define measurement as the comparison of an unknown quantity with a known fixed quantity consisting of a number and a unit

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Non-Standard Body Units
nodes.outcome: Identify handspan, cubit, foot, and pace as traditional body-based units of length

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Inconsistency of Non-Standard Units
nodes.outcome: Explain why body-based units vary between individuals and create the need for standard units

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: SI Unit of Length
nodes.outcome: State the metre (m) as the standard SI unit of length

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Metre to Centimetre and Millimetre Conversion
nodes.outcome: Calculate length conversions between metres, centimetres (1 m = 100 cm), and millimetres (1 cm = 10 mm)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Kilometre to Metre Conversion
nodes.outcome: Convert large distances between kilometres and metres (1 km = 1000 m)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Selecting Appropriate Measuring Tools
nodes.outcome: Select an appropriate measuring instrument (metre scale, measuring tape, or small ruler) based on the object's size and shape

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Proper Ruler Alignment
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate placing the scale in complete contact and parallel along the length being measured

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Measuring with Damaged Zero Mark
nodes.outcome: Calculate correct length when starting from a non-zero mark by subtracting the initial reading from the final reading

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Avoiding Parallax Error
nodes.outcome: Identify the correct eye position directly above the point of measurement to avoid parallax errors

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Measuring Curved Lines Using Thread
nodes.outcome: Measure the length of a curved line by tracing it with a non-stretchable thread and measuring the straightened thread on a scale

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Rest and Motion with Respect to Time
nodes.outcome: Distinguish between objects at rest and objects in motion based on whether their position changes over time

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Rectilinear Motion Definition
nodes.outcome: Define rectilinear motion as the movement of an object along a straight line path

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Examples of Rectilinear Motion
nodes.outcome: Classify real-world examples (march past of soldiers, falling stone, car on straight road) as rectilinear motion

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Circular Motion Definition
nodes.outcome: Define circular motion as the movement of an object along a circular path such that its distance from a fixed point remains constant

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Examples of Circular Motion
nodes.outcome: Classify movements such as the tip of a clock hand, blades of a ceiling fan, and a stone tied to a string as circular motion

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Periodic Motion Definition
nodes.outcome: Define periodic motion as motion that repeats itself at regular, equal intervals of time

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Examples of Periodic Motion
nodes.outcome: Classify movements such as a swinging pendulum, tree branch in wind, guitar string, and surface of a tabla as periodic motion

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Comparing Types of Motion
nodes.outcome: Compare rectilinear, circular, and periodic motions based on trajectory and repetition characteristics

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Simultaneous Combination of Motions
nodes.outcome: Identify combinations of motion in single objects, such as a rolling ball (rectilinear and rotational) or a sewing machine needle and wheel

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Luminous Objects Definition
nodes.outcome: Define luminous objects as objects that emit their own light

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Classify Luminous and Non-Luminous
nodes.outcome: Classify everyday objects as luminous or non-luminous

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Light Requirement for Vision
nodes.outcome: State that light is essential to see non-luminous objects around us

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Optical Medium Types
nodes.outcome: Differentiate between transparent, opaque, and translucent materials based on how light passes through them

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Straight-Line Travel of Light
nodes.outcome: State the principle that light travels along straight lines (rectilinear propagation)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Bent Pipe Light Demonstration
nodes.outcome: Explain why a candle flame is visible through a straight pipe but not through a bent pipe

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Concept of a Shadow
nodes.outcome: Define a shadow as a dark patch formed when an opaque object blocks the path of light

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Three Requirements for a Shadow
nodes.outcome: List the three requirements for shadow formation: a source of light, an opaque object, and a screen

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Role of Screen in Shadows
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate that a shadow cannot be observed without a screen behind the object

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Color of Shadows
nodes.outcome: Identify that the color of a shadow is always dark regardless of the color of the object

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Information Provided by Shadows
nodes.outcome: Explain why shadows give information only about the outline of an object and may sometimes mislead about its true shape

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Factors Affecting Shadow Size
nodes.outcome: Predict how the size of a shadow changes when the distances between the source, object, and screen are varied

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Pinhole Camera Working Principle
nodes.outcome: Explain how straight-line propagation of light allows a tiny aperture to form an image

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Construct a Pinhole Camera
nodes.outcome: Describe the construction of a sliding two-box pinhole camera using cardboard and tracing paper screen

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Characteristics of Pinhole Images
nodes.outcome: Identify that a pinhole camera forms an inverted and colored image of distant luminous or brightly lit objects

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Natural Pinhole Camera under Trees
nodes.outcome: Explain how circular patches of light seen under a leafy tree are pinhole images of the sun

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Observe Eclipse via Pinhole
nodes.outcome: Describe how a pinhole camera is safely used to view the changing shape of the sun during a solar eclipse

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Definition of Reflection
nodes.outcome: Define reflection of light as the change in direction of light upon striking a surface

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Light Redirection by a Plane Mirror
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate that a plane mirror redirects a beam of light in a specific new straight-line direction

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Comb and Mirror Light Pattern Experiment
nodes.outcome: Trace the pattern of light rays passing through a comb and reflecting off a flat mirror placed on thermocol

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Characteristics of Mirror Images
nodes.outcome: Identify that a plane mirror produces an erect, same-sized, and colored image of an object

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Compare Shadows and Reflections
nodes.outcome: Compare a shadow and a mirror reflection in terms of color, details shown, and mechanism of formation

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Compare Pinhole and Mirror Images
nodes.outcome: Compare an image formed by a pinhole camera (inverted) with an image formed by a plane mirror (erect)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Uses and Sources of Electricity
nodes.outcome: List common appliances powered by electricity and identify the electric cell and power stations as sources of electric current

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Terminals of an Electric Cell
nodes.outcome: Identify the positive terminal (metal cap) and negative terminal (metal disc) of a standard electric cell

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Chemical Action in Electric Cell
nodes.outcome: State that an electric cell produces electricity from chemicals stored inside it and stops working when these chemicals are exhausted

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Structure of a Torch Bulb
nodes.outcome: Identify the glass chamber, filament, supporting thick wires, and two terminals of a miniature torch bulb

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Filament of a Bulb
nodes.outcome: Define the filament as the thin wire fixed inside the bulb that gives off light when electricity passes through it

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Terminals of a Torch Bulb
nodes.outcome: Locate the two non-touching terminals of a bulb: one at the metal base and the other at the metal tip at the centre of the base

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Concept of an Electric Circuit
nodes.outcome: Define an electric circuit as a complete, closed path for electric current to flow between the two terminals of an electric cell

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Direction of Electric Current
nodes.outcome: State that the convention for the direction of electric current in an external circuit is from the positive terminal to the negative terminal

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Closed vs Open Circuits
nodes.outcome: Distinguish between a closed circuit (continuous path, current flows) and an open circuit (broken path, current does not flow)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Predicting Circuit Continuity
nodes.outcome: Predict whether a bulb will glow given various wire arrangements connecting a cell to a bulb

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Cause of a Fused Bulb
nodes.outcome: Explain that a bulb is fused when its filament is broken, which creates a break in the path of the electric current preventing it from glowing

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Assembling a Simple Torch
nodes.outcome: Construct a working home-made torch using an electric cell, a bulb, and a connecting wire

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Function of an Electric Switch
nodes.outcome: Define an electric switch as a simple device that is used to either break the electric circuit or complete it

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Safety Pin Switch Mechanism
nodes.outcome: Describe how a safety pin rotating across two drawing pins acts as an ON/OFF switch in a model circuit

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Tracing Torch Internal Circuit
nodes.outcome: Trace the path of electric current in the cross-sectional diagram of a commercial torch from cells through sliding switch to the bulb

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Direct Cell Terminal Connection Hazard
nodes.outcome: State why directly connecting the two terminals of an electric cell with a wire without a bulb or load discharges the cell extremely fast and is unsafe

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Conduction Tester Circuit
nodes.outcome: Design a conduction tester circuit with two free wire ends to test whether a given sample conducts electricity

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Definition of Electrical Conductors
nodes.outcome: Define electrical conductors as materials that allow electric current to pass through them easily

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Definition of Electrical Insulators
nodes.outcome: Define electrical insulators as materials that do not allow electric current to pass through them

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Classifying Conductors and Insulators
nodes.outcome: Classify common items (e.g., key, eraser, scale, matchstick, glass bangle, iron nail) into conductors and insulators using experimental tester results

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Metallic Nature of Conductors
nodes.outcome: Generalise that metals (copper, aluminium, iron) are generally good conductors of electricity

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Purpose of Wire Insulation
nodes.outcome: Explain why connecting wires have a metallic inner core and an outer covering of plastic or rubber

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Insulation on Electrical Tools
nodes.outcome: Explain why handles of screwdrivers and plier grips used by electricians are covered with rubber or plastic

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Human Body as a Conductor and Electrical Safety
nodes.outcome: Identify the human body as a conductor of electricity and deduce safety precautions needed when handling electrical appliances

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Discovery of Magnets
nodes.outcome: Narrate the discovery of natural magnets by the shepherd Magnus in ancient Greece

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Magnetite as Natural Magnet
nodes.outcome: Identify magnetite as a naturally occurring magnetic rock containing iron

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Shapes of Artificial Magnets
nodes.outcome: Identify common shapes of artificial magnets including bar, horse-shoe, cylindrical, and ball-ended magnets

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Magnetic Materials Definition
nodes.outcome: Define magnetic materials as those materials that get attracted towards a magnet

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Non-Magnetic Materials Definition
nodes.outcome: Define non-magnetic materials as those materials that are not attracted towards a magnet

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Common Magnetic Metals
nodes.outcome: List iron, nickel, and cobalt as common magnetic materials

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Classify Materials by Magnetism
nodes.outcome: Classify everyday objects as magnetic or non-magnetic using a test magnet

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Finding Iron Particles in Soil
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate the presence of iron particles in soil or sand by rolling a magnet in it

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Poles Concentration with Iron Filings
nodes.outcome: Observe that iron filings spread on a sheet cling mostly near the two ends of a bar magnet

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Definition of Magnetic Poles
nodes.outcome: Define magnetic poles as the two end regions of a magnet where magnetic attraction is strongest

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Suspended Magnet Alignment
nodes.outcome: State that a freely suspended bar magnet always comes to rest pointing in a North-South direction

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identifying North and South Poles
nodes.outcome: Identify the North-seeking pole as the North pole and the South-seeking pole as the South pole of a magnet

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Finding Geographic Directions
nodes.outcome: Determine the four cardinal directions (North, South, East, West) at a given place using a suspended magnet and the morning sun

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Structure of a Magnetic Compass
nodes.outcome: Describe the construction of a magnetic compass including its dial, glass cover, and pivoted magnetic needle

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Using a Magnetic Compass
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate how to find directions using a magnetic compass by rotating the case until the needle aligns with the North-South markings

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Single-Touch Magnetisation Method
nodes.outcome: Create a temporary magnet from an iron strip by stroking it repeatedly in one direction with a single pole of a bar magnet

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Making a Floating Needle Compass
nodes.outcome: Construct a simple compass by floating a magnetised sewing needle inserted in a cork or foam piece in a bowl of water

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Repulsion Between Like Poles
nodes.outcome: State and observe that like magnetic poles (N-N or S-S) repel each other

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Attraction Between Unlike Poles
nodes.outcome: State and observe that unlike magnetic poles (N-S or S-N) attract each other

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Predicting Pole Interactions
nodes.outcome: Predict whether two magnets will attract or repel given the orientation of their facing poles

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Repulsion as Sure Test of Magnetism
nodes.outcome: Explain why repulsion, and not attraction, is the sure test for identifying whether an object is a magnet

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Causes of Loss of Magnetism
nodes.outcome: Identify heating, hammering, and dropping from a height as actions that cause a magnet to lose its magnetic properties

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Storing Bar Magnets with Keepers
nodes.outcome: Explain how to store bar magnets in pairs with opposite poles alongside, separated by wood, with soft iron pieces across their ends

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Safe Handling Near Electronic Devices
nodes.outcome: State precautions for keeping magnets away from cassettes, mobiles, televisions, music systems, and computers to prevent damage

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Atmosphere Definition
nodes.outcome: Define atmosphere as the thin blanket of air surrounding the Earth.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Air Occupies Space
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate that air occupies space using an inverted bottle submerged in water.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Air Trapped in Soil
nodes.outcome: Show that soil contains trapped air by observing bubbles when water is added to a lump of dry soil.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Dissolved Air in Water
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate that water contains dissolved air by observing tiny bubbles forming on the inner surface of a heated pan before boiling.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Air Physical Properties
nodes.outcome: Identify that air is colourless, transparent, and cannot be seen but only felt when in motion.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Wind Definition
nodes.outcome: Define wind as moving air and identify everyday examples of its effects.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Air as a Mixture
nodes.outcome: State that air is not a single substance but a mixture of many gases, water vapour, and dust particles.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Water Vapour in Air
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate the presence of water vapour in air using droplets condensing on the outer surface of a glass containing ice-cold water.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Oxygen Supports Combustion
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate that oxygen supports burning using a candle extinguished by covering it with an inverted glass tumbler.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Nitrogen in Air
nodes.outcome: Identify nitrogen as the major component of air that does not support combustion and remains after a candle extinguishes in a sealed space.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Carbon Dioxide in Air
nodes.outcome: Identify that carbon dioxide is produced during the burning of materials and by respiration in living organisms.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Dust and Smoke in Air
nodes.outcome: Identify the presence of dust and smoke in air by observing a beam of sunlight in a dark room.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Composition of Air
nodes.outcome: List the approximate percentage composition of major gases in clean air: 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, and 1% carbon dioxide, water vapour, and other gases.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Nasal Hair and Mucus Function
nodes.outcome: Explain why breathing through the nose is safer than through the mouth, citing the filtration role of fine hairs and mucus.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Oxygen Cylinders at High Altitudes
nodes.outcome: Explain why mountaineers carry oxygen cylinders by referencing the reduced availability of air at higher altitudes in the atmosphere.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Respiration in Aquatic Organisms
nodes.outcome: Explain how aquatic animals and plants use oxygen dissolved in water for respiration.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Respiration of Organisms in Soil
nodes.outcome: Explain why organisms living in soil (such as earthworms) come out to the surface during heavy rains due to water filling air spaces in the soil.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Oxygen Production in Photosynthesis
nodes.outcome: Identify that plants produce more oxygen during photosynthesis than they consume during respiration.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Oxygen-Carbon Dioxide Balance
nodes.outcome: Trace the interdependence between plants and animals that maintains the balance of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Functions of Windmills
nodes.outcome: List applications of windmills, including drawing water from tubewells, running flour mills, and generating electricity.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Role of Air in Transport
nodes.outcome: Describe how air movements assist the movement of sailing yachts, gliders, parachutes, and aeroplanes.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Role of Air in the Water Cycle
nodes.outcome: Explain the role of air movement in the water cycle by carrying evaporated water vapour upward to form clouds.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Air in Seed Dispersal and Pollination
nodes.outcome: Explain how wind aids in the dispersal of seeds and the pollination of flowers in different plants.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Air as Medium for Sound
nodes.outcome: Identify that air acts as a medium that allows birds to fly and sounds to travel to our ears.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Daily domestic uses of water
nodes.outcome: List routine household activities that require water, such as drinking, cooking, bathing, washing, and cleaning

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Estimate daily household water consumption
nodes.outcome: Calculate the approximate total volume of water used daily by a family based on individual activity estimates

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Indirect water use in production
nodes.outcome: Identify indirect uses of water required to produce everyday goods like food crops, paper, and clothing

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Primary sources of water
nodes.outcome: List primary sources of freshwater and domestic supply, including rivers, ponds, lakes, springs, wells, and tube wells

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Saline ocean water vs freshwater
nodes.outcome: Distinguish between saline ocean water and freshwater in terms of fitness for direct drinking and irrigation

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Evaporation from water bodies and wet surfaces
nodes.outcome: Explain how water evaporates from oceans, rivers, soil, and wet clothes into the air as invisible water vapour

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Evaporation in sunlight versus shade
nodes.outcome: Compare the rates of water evaporation in open sunlight versus in shade and explain why warm air enables evaporation everywhere

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Transpiration contributing to water vapour
nodes.outcome: State that plants release large quantities of water vapour into the atmosphere through the process of transpiration

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Condensation on cold surface experiment
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate that water vapour condenses into water droplets on the outer surface of a glass containing ice cubes

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Cloud formation through cooling and condensation
nodes.outcome: Explain how air cools as it rises high up in the atmosphere, causing water vapour to condense around tiny particles to form clouds

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Forms of precipitation
nodes.outcome: Identify rain, hail, and snow as forms of precipitation resulting from coalescing droplets inside clouds

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Sequence of the water cycle
nodes.outcome: Trace the cyclic movement of water from Earth's surface to the atmosphere via evaporation and transpiration, and back via precipitation

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Surface runoff of rain and snowmelt
nodes.outcome: Trace how rainwater and melting mountain snow flow down as streams and rivers into lakes and ultimately return to the oceans

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Seepage of rainwater into groundwater
nodes.outcome: Explain how rainwater seeps through soil and rocks to become stored as groundwater

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Groundwater extraction methods
nodes.outcome: Identify open wells, tube wells, and hand pumps as mechanisms to draw usable groundwater to the surface

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Effect of concrete paving on seepage
nodes.outcome: Explain why extensive concrete paving and reduction of open soil reduce rainwater seepage and lower groundwater levels

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Causes of floods from heavy rainfall
nodes.outcome: State that excessive or prolonged rainfall causes water levels in rivers, lakes, and ponds to overflow their banks, resulting in floods

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Impacts of floods on life and environment
nodes.outcome: Describe the consequences of floods, including crop submergence, property damage, displacement of people, and harm to terrestrial and aquatic animals

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Mechanism leading to drought
nodes.outcome: Explain how continuous evaporation and transpiration without replenishment by rain over a year or more leads to severe drying of soil and water bodies

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Impacts of droughts on life and agriculture
nodes.outcome: Describe the consequences of drought, including depletion of groundwater, scarcity of food and fodder (famine), and loss of livestock

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Need for water conservation
nodes.outcome: Explain why water conservation is essential given the limited usable freshwater fraction and rising population demand

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Everyday water-saving practices
nodes.outcome: List practical everyday measures to save water, including turning off running taps, repairing leaks promptly, and reusing rinse water for gardening

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Rooftop rainwater harvesting system
nodes.outcome: Explain how rainwater collected from building rooftops is routed through pipes and filters to storage tanks or recharge pits

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Roadside runoff rainwater harvesting
nodes.outcome: Describe how roadside storm runoff is directed directly into roadside drains and ground percolation pits to recharge aquifers
